newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-COCOA CALLED LOWER BUT SUPPORT SEEN INTACT.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-COCOA CALLED LOWER BUT SUPPORT SEEN INTACT.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa futures are expected to open lower after trade selling weakened the New York market, but support at 1,010 stg basis September should remain intact, traders and analysts said on Wednesday.
The London market was called to open between 15 and 18 stg down from Tuesday's close.

Market sources said currency movements were less of a factor for the London cocoa market as sterling appeared to be trading in narrow ranges against the dollar and was building a base after last week's decline.
LIFFE cocoa ended higher on Tuesday as early rises in New York and easier sterling triggered a succession of buy stops.
But then a bout of trade selling pummelled New York's Sept/Dec spread as traders concentrated on adjusting positions before first notice day on August 18, the start of the September delivery period.
Technical analysts said support for London's September contract appeared fairly solid at 1,010 stg and there was still the potential to push higher given the break above initial resistance at 1,030.

"Support is mainly at 1,010 and it's unlikely to be tested," said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst. The next resistance point was placed at 1,063 one of a series of peaks notched up last month.
Short-term momentum indicators were pushing higher into positive territory, suggesting prices were retaining their upside potential.
Traders have also said the latest forecast for the Ivory Coast 1997/98 main crop could be adding to the bearish sentiment.
An unnamed industry analyst said on Tuesday that the crop could reach up to 1.1 million tonnes, depending on the weather over the next four to five weeks.
The forecast, which was based on pod counts including developing fruits, showed a 1997/98 main crop similar or slightly above 1996/97 levels.
